original_question: Does there exist a finite abelian group G for which the set Delta*(G) = {min Delta(G0) : G0 subset G and Delta(G0) is nonempty} is an interval and, at the same time, the exponent of G is at least 2r(G) + 2, where r(G) is the rank of G?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Theorem 1.1(2): the characterization of when Δ*(H) (equivalently Δ*(G)) is an interval.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main invariant Δ*(G), the interval question, and the exponent/rank regime in which the interval property is subtle. It also keeps the scope on finite abelian groups, which is the right ambient class.
missing_details: The paper’s statement is not merely existential; it gives a full characterization of when Δ*(H) (hence Δ*(G)) is an interval.

The paper works first with a Krull monoid H with finite class group G such that every class contains a prime divisor; one then identifies Δ*(H)=Δ*(B(G)), so a group-only reformulation must make that passage explicit.
You need the paper’s auxiliary parameter k, defined as the maximal integer such that G has a subgroup isomorphic to C_n^k, where n=exp(G).
You should define n=exp(G) and r=r(G) explicitly.
You should define Δ*(G) in the zero-sum-sequence sense used by the paper: Δ*(G)={min Δ(G0): G0⊂G, Δ(G0)≠∅}, where Δ(G0) is the set of distances of the monoid B(G0) of zero-sum sequences over G0.
You should specify that an interval means a finite discrete interval [a,b]∩Z.
The exceptional family G≅C_{2r+2}^r is missing; it is essential to the exact criterion.
Your inequality exp(G)≥2r(G)+2 is only a special slice of the paper’s actual condition, which is expressed in terms of r, n, and k.
The paper gives several equivalent formulations of the interval property; your draft omits these equivalent conditions, especially max{1,n-k-2}∈Δ*(G).
Because the paper proves an exact iff statement, a faithful stand-alone question should ask for that equivalence, not just whether some example exists.
refined_question: Let G be a finite abelian group with |G|≥3, set n=exp(G) and r=r(G), and let k be maximal such that G contains a subgroup isomorphic to C_n^k. Define Δ*(G)={min Δ(G0): G0⊂G and Δ(G0)≠∅}, where Δ(G0) is the set of distances of the monoid B(G0) of zero-sum sequences over G0. Is it true that Δ*(G) is an interval if and only if either r+k≥n−1, or r+k=n−2 and G≅C_{2r+2}^r?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, with the same notation, is Δ*(G) an interval if and only if max{1,n−k−2} belongs to Δ*(G)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s interval problem for the set of minimal distances, but it asks only for existence in one narrow parameter range. The exact paper-faithful formulation is the full characterization in Theorem 1.1(2), which gives four equivalent conditions for Δ*(H) to be an interval. Nearby context defines n=exp(G), r=r(G), and the crucial parameter k, and Section 2 explains that transfer to B(G) lets one restate the theorem purely in terms of the finite abelian group G. Your condition exp(G)≥2r(G)+2 isolates only a special regime of that theorem and suppresses the indispensable exceptional case G≅C_{2r+2}^r. So the draft is directionally right, but incomplete and substantially weaker than the paper’s actual statement.
